decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom required heavy development investment and was publicly announced for 2019 release, and the weaker 2019 web presence can still be attributed to the slow particle therapy market and regulatory timing, so management would persist rather than write it off.

Small volume chambers are core dosimetry products with ongoing calibration and accessory revenue and kept a dedicated page, so dropping one would gain little and contradict the firm's dosimetry positioning.
Although it partly overlaps with Product B, it was launched and shown visibly as part of the firm's dosimetry portfolio, and the low cost of keeping it in the catalog favors persistence.
The standard clinical chamber line with several models is a central, heavily invested workhorse of the reference dosimetry business and is unlikely to be withdrawn.
The relative dosimetry chamber complements the firm's water phantom and scanning systems, so it stays embedded in the integrated QA workflow the firm has publicly committed to.
Thimble chambers are staple, long-lived dosimetry devices with stable demand and accredited calibration support, so there is no compelling reason to drop it.
